_format: Slice 10a py-framework ground truth. Written BEFORE the resolver, per the discipline that has already won disagreements in 5d-ii, 9a and 9b. Where the implementation and this file disagree, this file is the claim to argue against — not the thing to edit.
_endpoint: Each entry is one Endpoint entity and its SERVED_BY target. `address` is the entity name, which is what FTS5 tokenises. `path` is the DECLARED path: no prefix from APIRouter(prefix=...) or Blueprint registration is composed in, because composing it needs a fact from another file and a wrong URL is worse than a partial one.
_forbidden: Endpoints that must NEVER exist. Each is a specific wrong answer a plausible implementation would produce. These are checked BEFORE the set-equality assertion, because Slice 9a found that a forbidden list sitting behind set equality is unreachable and never fires.

forbidden.why: APIRouter(prefix='/v1') composed into the declared path. The prefix only applies if some other file calls include_router, which this fixture does not contain.
A Blueprint url_prefix composed into the path.
`cache` is bound to Cache(), not to a framework constructor. Matching on the decorator's spelling finds this.
A class literally named Router is still not fastapi.APIRouter.
A module-level function named `get` used as a decorator factory.
A dict subscript call that resembles an Express registration.
PREFIX + '/items' evaluated. Nerve does not evaluate expressions.
A lambda has no entity to serve, so there is no target for the edge.
`app` is imported from another module. Emitting this requires cross-module value tracking, which is the stated lower bound.
The decorator is a subscript, not a dotted name. Emitted by nothing and counted by nothing.
`methods=METHODS` is a name. Flask's default GET must not be applied when an unreadable methods argument is present — that would invent a method the source did not state.

_unsupported_by_form: Every construct Nerve read and declined, counted by form. The gate asserts this map exactly, so a new unreadable form cannot appear silently. `app-not-local` is the cross-module limit. A `decorator-form` member was drafted and REMOVED: making it fire needed a special case whose only purpose was to feed the counter, it contradicted the rule that Nerve counts nothing when it has no reason to think a construct is a route, and 9a already counts unsupported decorator shapes.
_ambiguous: Declarations the source really does make twice. Both edges are kept; the ambiguity is reported rather than resolved by choosing one.
_known_false_negatives: Routes a human can see and Nerve does not record. Asserted ABSENT, so an FN cannot be quietly 'fixed' by a guess — promoting one has to be a deliberate change to this file. Mechanism introduced in Slice 9b.

known_false_negatives.reason: app-not-local: the binding proving `app` is a FastAPI instance is in fastapi_app.py. Following it is cross-module value tracking, not a binding lookup.
path-not-literal: PREFIX + '/items' requires evaluating an expression. Recording the operand text would be a guess at the address.
handler-not-a-symbol: `app.get('/lambda')(lambda: [])` registers a callable that is not a declared symbol, so no entity can be the target.

_not_a_route: Symbols in the fixture that must have NO incoming SERVED_BY edge at all. A control against a rule that attaches endpoints too eagerly.
_gates: 1. Every entry in `resolved` exists, with exactly the stated address, handler and handler kind.
2. No entry in `forbidden` exists. Checked FIRST, so it cannot hide behind set equality.
3. Nothing in `not_a_route` has an incoming SERVED_BY edge.
5. `unsupported_by_form` matches exactly — no new form, no changed count.
6. The endpoint set is exactly `resolved`: FP = 0 and FN = 0 beyond the declared ones.
7. FastAPI and Flask are reported as SEPARATE tables and never summed into one score.
8. Every SERVED_BY observation carries FRAMEWORK_RULE / DIRECT and extractor id py-framework.
9. No py-framework observation carries a relation other than SERVED_BY, asserted over Relation::ALL.
10. negative.py contributes zero endpoints AND zero unsupported counts — Nerve does not know those are routes, so a tally would itself be a false claim.
